questions.title: Beta-Binomial conjugate posterior and predictive moments
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation grounded in Persi Diaconis and Donald Ylvisaker, Conjugate Priors for Exponential Families, The Annals of Statistics 7 (1979), 269-281, DOI 10.1214/aos/1176344611. Let theta have a Beta(alpha,beta) prior with alpha>0 and beta>0. Given theta, observe S successes in n conditionally independent Bernoulli trials, where n is a nonnegative integer and 0<=S<=n. Develop one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX derivation of the Beta(alpha+S,beta+n-S) posterior, its exact mean and variance, and the Beta-Binomial posterior predictive distribution for Y successes in m future Bernoulli trials. Derive the predictive probability mass function, mean, and variance using conditional expectation and variance; distinguish posterior uncertainty from a plug-in Binomial model. Establish success-failure exchange symmetry, sequential updating coherence, the no-data boundary, and the one-future-trial predictive boundary. The required model-authored artifact is est_beta_binomial_posterior and must implement run_estimator(request) exactly for the frozen public contract. Exploratory Python or R may check identities. A separately frozen confirmatory assessment draws from the posterior and posterior predictive distribution at predeclared inputs and compares empirical moments with the exact formulas using Monte Carlo uncertainty. Source-code replication and novelty are not applicable. Lean formalization is not applicable to this focused nonformal capability task.

request_fields.name: successes
request_fields.meaning: The observed number S of Bernoulli successes.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonintegers, negative values, and values larger than trials.

request_fields.name: trials
request_fields.meaning: The observed number n of conditionally independent Bernoulli trials.
request_fields.edge_cases: Zero is allowed for the no-data boundary; reject booleans, nonintegers, and negative values.

request_fields.name: prior_alpha
request_fields.meaning: The strictly positive finite alpha shape parameter of the Beta prior for theta.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite values, zero, and negative values.

request_fields.name: prior_beta
request_fields.meaning: The strictly positive finite beta shape parameter of the Beta prior for theta.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite values, zero, and negative values.

request_fields.name: future_trials
request_fields.meaning: The fixed number m of future conditionally independent Bernoulli trials in the posterior predictive experiment.
request_fields.edge_cases: Zero is allowed and must give zero predictive mean and variance; reject booleans, nonintegers, and negative values.

response_fields.name: posterior_alpha
response_fields.meaning: The exact posterior success-side shape alpha+S.
response_fields.edge_cases: Equals prior_alpha when successes is zero.

response_fields.name: posterior_beta
response_fields.meaning: The exact posterior failure-side shape beta+n-S.
response_fields.edge_cases: Equals prior_beta when every observed trial succeeds.

response_fields.name: posterior_mean
response_fields.shape: finite scalar strictly between zero and one
response_fields.edge_cases: Uses the prior mean when trials is zero.
response_fields.normalization: posterior_alpha divided by posterior_alpha plus posterior_beta.

response_fields.name: posterior_variance
response_fields.edge_cases: Remains positive for every admitted finite input.
response_fields.normalization: a*b divided by (a+b)^2*(a+b+1), for posterior shapes a and b.

response_fields.name: predictive_mean
response_fields.meaning: The exact posterior predictive expectation E(Y|S,n) for future_trials=m.
response_fields.shape: finite scalar between zero and m
response_fields.edge_cases: Equals zero when future_trials is zero.

response_fields.name: predictive_variance
response_fields.meaning: The exact posterior predictive variance Var(Y|S,n) after integrating over theta.
response_fields.edge_cases: Equals zero for m=0 and posterior_mean*(1-posterior_mean) for m=1.
response_fields.normalization: m*a*b*(a+b+m) divided by (a+b)^2*(a+b+1), for posterior shapes a and b.

invariants.meaning: Posterior shapes equal prior_alpha+successes and prior_beta+trials-successes exactly, and all returned moments use those same shapes.

Replacing successes by trials-successes and swapping prior_alpha with prior_beta swaps posterior shapes, changes posterior_mean to one minus its original value, preserves posterior and predictive variances, and changes predictive_mean to future_trials minus its original value.
Updating on two batches sequentially by using the first posterior shapes as the second prior gives the same posterior and predictive moments as one pooled update.
When trials and successes are zero, posterior shapes and posterior moments equal their prior counterparts.
For future_trials=1, predictive_mean equals posterior_mean and predictive_variance equals posterior_mean times one minus posterior_mean.

empirical_claims.meaning: At each frozen admitted input, independent Beta draws from the exact posterior have empirical mean and variance compatible with the returned posterior moments up to declared Monte Carlo uncertainty.

At each frozen admitted input, independent posterior-predictive counts generated by first drawing theta from the posterior and then a Binomial count have empirical mean and variance compatible with the returned predictive moments up to declared Monte Carlo uncertainty.

For every frozen future horizon m>1, the returned predictive variance exceeds the plug-in Binomial variance m*posterior_mean*(1-posterior_mean), reflecting posterior uncertainty rather than being silently replaced by a plug-in model.
Every confirmatory setting supplies the exact frozen counts, prior shapes, and future horizon and verifies the public posterior and predictive formulas before aggregating Monte Carlo outcomes.
